text: If, therefore, you would rather please than offend, rather be well than ill spoken of, rather be loved than hated; remember to have that constant attention about you which flatters every man's little vanity; and the want of which, by mortifying his pride, never fails to excite his resentment, or at least his ill will.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter I, to his son, Bath, October 9, Old Style 1746
